title: Surrounded Regions
summary: Given an m x n matrix board with 'X' and 'O', capture regions surrounded by 'X' on all sides.
statement: Given an m x n matrix board with 'X' and 'O', capture regions surrounded by 'X' on all sides. Connect adjacent 'O's to form regions. If a region is surrounded by 'X' and not on the edge, replace all 'O's in that region with 'X's in-place.
constraints: The rectangular board has 1–200 rows and 1–200 columns and contains only 'X' and 'O'.
Only horizontal and vertical neighbors connect. Any O region connected to any board edge stays O, even if some of its cells are far inside the board. Diagonal contact does not connect regions.
Change surrounded O cells to X in the original board. Return nothing; the judge checks the mutated board, not a returned copy.
target_space_complexity: O(rows × columns) for the explicit stack
hints: Ask which O cells cannot be captured: those connected to an edge.
Flood-fill from every edge O and temporarily mark all reachable O cells as protected.
Push unmarked edge O cells, repeatedly mark/push their four O neighbors, then restore marked cells to O and change remaining O cells to X.
Mark before pushing so each cell is processed once. Use an explicit stack for large grids; recursive DFS expresses the same idea but can exceed Python's recursion limit.
editorial: A region is captured exactly when it has no path to the boundary. Reverse the question and explore only safe regions from all edge cells. The reference uses an explicit DFS stack and a temporary marker in the original board, then performs one final in-place sweep. This handles a 200×200 connected region without Python recursion overflow. The independent oracle does no boundary flood-fill: it unions adjacent O cells in a disjoint-set structure with an outside sentinel, then queries connectivity. This differs from island counting and flood-fill recoloring: only fully enclosed regions change, no seed cell is supplied, and the input board itself is the graded output.

tests.explanation: The three interior O cells have no route to an edge and become X. The bottom-row O touches the edge and stays O.
All O cells connect through up/down/left/right steps to the top-edge O, so the entire region stays unchanged.
